metadata.title: Discrepancy and local statistics of modular inverses

conventions.proof: A mathematical statement, identity, estimate or calculation used in the written proof.
conventions.method: Reuse of an argument or explicit method attribution, distinct from use of the source result's numerical conclusion.
conventions.literature: A trusted external result or definition at the locator recorded in the inventory.
conventions.source_locators: One-based lines in the identified v39 source; statement PDF pages are taken from its compiled auxiliary file.
conventions.synthetic_ids: The prefixes step:, external: and ov: identify repository records; they are not new manuscript labels or theorem numbers.
conventions.scope: Numbered statements and substantive supporting steps. Section 3 comparison calculations and Section 6 discussion remain separate from the main proof graph. Ambient definitions, arithmetic and analysis are described where used rather than expanded into a formal axiomatic foundation.
conventions.literature_policy: Cited literature results are treated as trusted inputs and are not reproved here. Their statements, hypotheses, parameter ranges, and normalizations must match each application. Explicit method credit is distinguished from an assumed external conclusion.
conventions.status_colours: Purple: trusted references. Green: certified internal entries. Yellow: pending certification. All internal entries are pending because formalization has not started; this status is separate from the mathematical audit.

sections.3: Fourier analysis of the point set
sections.4: Discrepancy of convex and well-shaped sets

nodes.title: Convex discrepancy with perimeter dependence
nodes.summary: For convex sets represented inside a translated unit square, bounds discrepancy by $X^{\varepsilon}(X^{-1}+P^{2/3}X^{-2/3})$, uniformly in the position and the set, for $X\ge2$.
notes: Includes degenerate convex sets, with the stated continuous perimeter convention and pointwise boundary membership.
The proof chooses different smoothing scales according as $P\ge X^{-1/2}$ or $P<X^{-1/2}$; the latter includes $P=0$.
The term $X^{-1}$ is retained. The coordinate-separation bound later gives more precise information for very short perimeters.

nodes.title: Isotropic discrepancy bound
nodes.summary: Taking the supremum over the manuscript's class of convex sets gives discrepancy $\ll_{\varepsilon}X^{-2/3+\varepsilon}$.
notes: Uses the uniform perimeter bound $P\le4$, as established in the proof of Lemma 2.7.

nodes.title: Relative counting for shrinking convex shapes
nodes.summary: For a fixed convex body of positive area and $0<\kappa<1/2$, obtains relative error $O_{K_0,\kappa}(X^{-\kappa})$ at dilations $t\ge X^{-1/2+\kappa}$ that fit inside a translated unit square, uniformly over translations and rotations.
notes: Uses area scaling by $t^2$ and perimeter scaling by $t$, then divides the absolute discrepancy bound by the area.

nodes.title: Discrepancy from topological boundary neighborhoods
nodes.summary: If $b_E(s)\le Bs^{\alpha}$ for $0<s\le1$, $0<\alpha\le1$ and $B\ge1$, gives $D_X(E)\ll_{\varepsilon}B^{2/(2+\alpha)}X^{-2\alpha/(2+\alpha)+\varepsilon}$ for $X\ge2$.
notes: The implied constant depends only on epsilon, uniformly in alpha, B and the measurable set E.
Uses the topological boundary and pointwise brackets, not an almost-everywhere representative.
It redoes the smoothing argument with a different boundary hypothesis. It is not a numerical consequence of Theorem 1.1 or Proposition 4.2.
The proof handles $B\ge X^{\alpha}$ trivially; otherwise it takes $\delta=(BX^2)^{-1/(2+\alpha)}/8$ and absorbs the remaining factors.

nodes.title: Distribution of ordered differences
nodes.summary: The difference measure, including diagonal pairs, has discrepancy $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(PX^{-1}+X^{-2})$ for a convex set of perimeter $P$ in a translated unit square. For a product of arcs of area $V$, the bound is $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(X^{-2}+V^{2/3}X^{-5/3})$, independently of its aspect ratio.
notes: The convex and product-of-arcs clauses have separate proofs.
The distinct-pair versions are stated after the theorem and follow by the separate diagonal-removal identity (5.4).
The box bound uses the rectangular frequency moment directly; the convex bound uses its squared shell consequence.

nodes.title: Variance of counts in translates
nodes.summary: The variance of the normalized count is $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(P^2X^{-2}+A^{4/3}P^{2/3}X^{-5/3})$ for a convex set with area $A$ and perimeter $P$. Products of arcs satisfy $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(VX^{-2}+V^{5/3}X^{-5/3})$, and discs satisfy $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(r^2X^{-2}+r^{10/3}X^{-5/3})$. If every translate contains at most one point, the variance equals $|E|/N_X-|E|^2$.
notes: The disc clause is obtained from the already proved convex clause; the component graph records that use without a self-edge on this theorem.
The exact identity is proved in Lemma 5.3 before the theorem's proof, despite its earlier appearance as equation (1.15).
The variance bounds do not require smoothing. The rectangle proof reuses a frequency-block method from the difference proof, not the numerical difference bound.

nodes.title: Moments of the distance to the point set
nodes.summary: For every fixed $s>0$, the $s$-th distance moment lies between constant multiples of $X^{-\vartheta(s)}$ and $X^{-\vartheta(s)+\varepsilon}$, where $\vartheta(s)=\min\{s,1+s/2\}$. Thus the exponents change at $s=2$.
notes: The upper bound depends on both Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.3 through the distance tail and a uniform cutoff.
The lower bounds use a finite-point packing argument and the explicitly empty rectangle (1.6).
At $s=2$, v39 determines the power of $X$ but no precise subpower factor or leading constant.

nodes.title: The BRS frequency second moment
nodes.summary: For all real $N,X\ge1$ and $\eta>0$, $\sum_{N\le|r|<2N}|A_X(r,1)|^2\ll_\eta(NX)^\eta(NX^2+N^{1/3}X^{7/3})$. Both signs are included, with no relation between $N$ and $X$.

references.role: Convention converting the source's small-power notation to a bound for every positive exponent

notes: The paragraph at line 383 explains the exponent convention and bounded parameter range. This is a fixed-height second moment; it is not the height-averaged theorem of the companion paper.
Equation (1.2) in the introduction repeats this result and is not a separate predecessor.

nodes.title: Cumulative frequency second moment
nodes.summary: For real $R,Y\ge1$, the sum over $1\le|r|\le R$ is $\ll_\eta(RY)^\eta(RY^2+R^{1/3}Y^{7/3})$.
notes: The upper endpoint is included even when R is a power of two.

nodes.title: Second moment over a frequency rectangle
nodes.summary: For $M,N,X\ge1$, $\sum_{|m|\le M,\ |n|\le N,\ (m,n)\ne(0,0)}|A_X(m,n)|^2\ll_\varepsilon(MNX)^\varepsilon\{MNX^2+(MN)^{1/3}X^{7/3}\}$. The axes and all signs are included.

references.role: Divisor bound used in the reduction

notes: The divisor restriction d<=min(M,N,X) ensures both parameters in Corollary 2.2 are at least one.
The introductory equation (1.17) is a restatement, not a prerequisite.

nodes.title: Normalized moments on frequency shells
nodes.summary: For $X\ge2$ and $H\ge1$, the shell $\ell^2$ norm is $\ll_\eta(HX)^\eta(X^{-1}H+X^{-5/6}H^{1/3})$. Its square is $\ll_\eta(HX)^\eta(X^{-2}H^2+X^{-5/3}H^{2/3})$, and $|a_X(k)|^2\le1$.
notes: The statement uses N_X>>X^2 for normalization. The arbitrary exponent is renamed after squaring.
The introductory equation (1.18) repeats the shell estimate.

nodes.title: Fourier tail from an L2 translation estimate
nodes.summary: If $g\in L^2(\mathbb T^2)$ satisfies $\|g(\cdot+h)-g\|_2^2\le\Lambda|h|_2^\alpha$ for $|h|_2\le1$, with $0<\alpha\le1$ and $\Lambda\ge0$, then $\sum_{\|k\|_\infty\ge H}|\widehat g(k)|^2\le 2^{-\alpha/2}\Lambda H^{-\alpha}/[2(1-1/\pi)]$ for every real $H\ge1$.
notes: The proof averages the translation multiplier on a square of side 1/H. It is independent of the arithmetic moment estimates.

nodes.title: Pointwise smooth brackets for measurable sets
nodes.summary: For measurable $E\subset\mathbb T^2$ and $0<\delta\le1/8$, constructs smooth real $f_-\le\mathbf1_E\le f_+$ at every point, with values in $[0,1]$. The integral error is at most $b_E(3\delta)$; Fourier coefficients and shell norms gain $(1+\delta H)^{-L}$ with boundary errors $b_E(3\delta)$ and $b_E(3\delta)^{1/2}$ respectively.

references.role: Fourier transform of convolution, recalled at line 477

notes: Uses the mollifier and basic Fourier facts from subsection 2.3, not the numerical conclusion of Lemma 2.5.
The mention of the counting identity at line 528 motivates the construction; Proposition 3.1 is not used to prove these brackets.

nodes.title: Boundary, translation and Fourier bounds for convex sets
nodes.summary: For convex $\Omega\subset u+[0,1)^2$, $E=\pi\Omega$, perimeter $P$ and area $A$, proves $b_E(s)\le4\pi(Ps+s^2)$, $\|\mathbf1_E(\cdot+h)-\mathbf1_E\|_2^2\le P|h|_2$, Fourier tail $\ll P/T$, and $|\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(k)|\le\min(A,P/(4|k|_2))$ for $k\ne0$. Degenerate convex sets are included.
notes: The Fourier-tail component uses Lemma 2.5 after the translation component has been proved; there is no self-dependency of the whole lemma.
Here |k|_2 is Euclidean length of the vector k, not the absolute value of its second coordinate.

nodes.title: Fourier estimates for convex brackets
nodes.summary: For $0<\delta\le1/8$ and $H\ge1$, with $b=P\delta+\delta^2$, the brackets have integral error $\ll b$, shell norm $\ll_L(1+\delta H)^{-L}(P^{1/2}H^{-1/2}+b^{1/2})$, and coefficient bound $\ll_L(1+\delta H)^{-L}(P/H+b)$.
notes: Combines the generic brackets with the tube, Fourier-tail and pointwise components of Lemma 2.7.

nodes.title: A boundary-tube bound implies a translation bound
nodes.summary: For any measurable $E$ with $b_E(s)\le C_0(Ps+s^2)$ for $0<s\le1$, subdivision of a translation gives $\|\mathbf1_E(\cdot+h)-\mathbf1_E\|_1\le C_0P|h|_2$ for $|h|_2<1$. The separate convex slicing argument supplies the sharper constant used in (2.20).
notes: Reuses the boundary-crossing argument from the proof of Lemma 2.6.
The references to Theorem 1.1 and to the convex bounds describe applications and comparisons; those conclusions are not prerequisites for the generic implication.

nodes.title: Fourier identities for counting, differences and variance
nodes.summary:
For $X\ge2$, smooth counting error is $\sum_{k
e0}\widehat f(k)a_X(k)$, smooth difference-distribution error is $\sum_{k
e0}\widehat f(k)|a_X(k)|^2$, and for every measurable $E$ the translation variance is $\sum_{k
e0}|\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(k)|^2|a_X(k)|^2$.

references.role: Smooth Fourier inversion recalled at line 477
Parseval for the measurable variance identity

notes: The identities need no BRS moment estimate, no shell bound, and no translation-to-tail lemma.
The introductory equations (1.19) and (1.20) announce these identities and do not constitute proof inputs.
Parts (i)-(iii) are recorded separately as auxiliary equation nodes for downstream use.

nodes.title: Variance as an average of the overlap function
nodes.summary: For $C_E(v)=\int\mathbf1_E(x)\mathbf1_E(x+v)\,dx$, direct expansion gives $\mathcal V_X(E)=\int C_E\,d\nu_X-|E|^2$. The variance theorem uses the Fourier variance identity directly, independently of the difference-distribution theorem.
notes: The equality is obtained by expanding the defining finite sum and changing variables; it does not require the conclusions of Theorems 1.5 or 1.6 or Proposition 3.1.

nodes.title: Dyadic sums against smoothing decay
nodes.summary: Controls the dyadic sum of $H^s(1+\delta H)^{-L}$ by $\delta^{-s}$ for $s>0$ and by a constant for $s<0$, with $L>\max(s,0)$ and $0<\delta\le1$.
notes: The statement excludes $s=0$.
Its proof gives explicit geometric-series constants and uniformity for s in compact subsets of $(0,L)$; the boundary proof separately treats the exponent that can cross zero.

nodes.title: Smoothing inequality for convex discrepancy
nodes.summary: At any $0<\delta\le1/8$, controls convex discrepancy by the boundary error $b=P\delta+\delta^2$ and the Fourier contributions with scales $X^{-1}\delta^{-1/2}$ and $X^{-5/6}$.
notes: Pairs the geometric shell norm from Corollary 2.8 with the arithmetic shell norm from Corollary 2.4.
The pointwise-bracket reduction is required because the counting measure is atomic.
The displayed bound holds for every eta>0; its proof first treats $0<\eta\le1/12$.

nodes.title: Elementary discrepancy from coordinate separation
nodes.summary: For convex sets in a translated unit square, gives the absolute-constant bound $D_X(\pi\Omega)\ll X^{-2}+\min(w_1,w_2)\ll X^{-2}+P(\Omega)$ for $X\ge2$.
notes: The counting argument is elementary; no second moment, smoothing estimate, or Theorem 1.1 is used.
Uses injectivity and denominator separation in each coordinate, the cardinality lower bound, and the direct geometric inequality $2w_j\le P$.
Works with lifts in the chosen square, including points whose coordinates acquire integer shifts.

nodes.title: Sharp discrepancy order for very small perimeters
nodes.summary: For real $X\ge4$ and $0\le p\le X^{-1}$, the largest discrepancy among convex sets of perimeter at most p has order $p+X^{-2}$, with absolute constants.
notes: The supremum includes segments and points; $p=0$ is explicitly covered.
The lower example is a diagonal segment containing reciprocal points. The real-height case follows by replacing X by floor(X).
Uses Proposition 4.3 for the upper bound, not Theorem 1.1.

nodes.title: A positive-area obstruction to deleting the baseline term
nodes.summary: A thin rectangle containing many diagonal reciprocal points has discrepancy $\gg X^{-1}$ while its perimeter contribution is $O(X^{-4/3})$, so the baseline term in Theorem 1.1 remains necessary even for positive-area convex bodies.
nodes.origin: Proved or explained in the remark
notes: The construction is for integer X and gives the asserted discrepancy lower bound for sufficiently large X.
This is a direct example using the elementary cardinality upper bound. It is not obtained by applying Theorem 1.1 or Corollary 4.4.

nodes.title: Discrepancy of well-shaped sets
nodes.summary: For the Euclidean definition of gamma-well-shapedness inside $[0,1)^2$, gives discrepancy $\ll_{\varepsilon}(1+\gamma)^{2/3}X^{-2/3+\varepsilon}$, uniformly for $\gamma\ge0$ and $X\ge2$.
notes: The proof first converts the Euclidean inner/outer neighborhood bounds into a topological-boundary tube bound on the torus.
The $1+\gamma$ factor accounts for the boundary strip of the fundamental square.
BRS Lemma 3.1 and equation (5.4), mentioned immediately before the corollary, are contextual comparisons and not proof inputs.

nodes.title: A fractal-boundary example beyond well-shaped sets
nodes.summary: Applies the boundary theorem to a Koch snowflake inside the unit square, with $\alpha=2-\log 4/\log 3$, giving exponent $0.539\ldots$; the same domain is not gamma-well-shaped for any finite gamma.
nodes.origin: Proved or explained in the remark

references.role: Koch construction, its bounded complementary domain, construction arcs and Minkowski dimension

notes: Uses the Koch construction and its Minkowski dimension from LP Section 1, then proves the needed tube upper bound by covering the construction arcs.
Failure of well-shapedness uses the linear tube bound established in the proof of Corollary 4.6 and the dimension of the boundary, not that corollary's discrepancy conclusion.
The torus-projection argument is repeated directly. The convex tube inequality is not applied to this nonconvex domain.

nodes.title: Why the boundary hypothesis is pointwise
nodes.summary: The finite set $E=\mathcal P_X$ has indicator zero almost everywhere but discrepancy one. Thus almost-everywhere or distributional-perimeter information cannot replace the stated pointwise/topological boundary control.
nodes.origin: Proved or explained in the remark
notes: This is a direct observation from the definitions of the counting measure and Lebesgue measure.
Theorem 1.4 and Lemma 2.6 are the statements being explained, not prerequisites used to prove the example.
Do not add theorem-to-remark or remark-to-bracket proof edges merely for this explanatory relationship.

nodes.title: Smooth pointwise brackets for arcs
nodes.summary: An arc of length $a$ admits smooth upper and lower brackets with integral error at most $4\delta$. With $a'=\min(1,a+4\delta)$, their coefficients are $\ll_L\min\{a',(1+|m|)^{-1}\}(1+\delta|m|)^{-L}$.
notes: The construction applies to the empty arc, a point, and the full circle, as well as ordinary arcs.
The pointwise construction adapts the proof of Lemma 2.6 to the circle; it does not use a two-dimensional lemma statement as a one-dimensional theorem.

nodes.title: Relative asymptotics for shrinking difference sets
nodes.summary: For $0<\kappa<1$, a fixed positive-area convex shape at linear scale $t\ge X^{-1+\kappa}$ has relative difference-count error $O(X^{-\kappa/2})$, uniformly in position and orientation within a translated unit square. Products of arcs have the same error when their area is at least $X^{-2+\kappa}$. Both conclusions hold with and without diagonal pairs under the corresponding normalizations.
notes: The distinct-pair clauses also use the separate diagonal-removal estimate (5.4).

nodes.title: Exact variance for sets containing at most one point in each translate
nodes.summary: If every translate of a measurable set contains at most one point, its normalized-count variance is $|E|/N_X-|E|^2$. A sufficient condition is containment, after projection, in a strip of width below $X^{-2}$; the stated small-perimeter, narrow-rectangle and small-disc cases follow.
notes: The identity is proved directly from the two possible count values, without invoking Theorem 1.6.
The sufficient condition uses the coordinate separation and width arguments proved with Proposition 4.3.

nodes.title: Small exceptional sets for translates of shrinking convex shapes
nodes.summary: For a fixed positive-area convex shape at scale $t\ge X^{-1+\kappa}$, the centers with relative count error greater than $\lambda$ have measure $\ll_{K_0,\kappa}\lambda^{-2}X^{-3\kappa/2}$, uniformly over admissible rotations and scales, for $0<\kappa<1$ and $0<\lambda\le1$.
notes: The exceptional set may depend on the chosen shape, orientation and scale; this corollary does not assert one set for every orientation or scale.

nodes.title: One exceptional set for a range of disc radii
nodes.summary: For $r_0\le r\le1/4$, a single exceptional set has measure $\ll_\varepsilon\lambda^{-3}X^\varepsilon(X^{-2}r_0^{-2}+X^{-5/3}r_0^{-2/3})$ and outside it every disc count has relative error $O(\lambda)$. Open and closed discs are included. Taking $r_0=X^{-1+\kappa}$ and $\lambda=X^{-\kappa/3}$ yields exceptional measure $\ll_\kappa X^{-\kappa/2}$ for sufficiently large $X$.
notes: The extra factor $\lambda^{-1}$ comes from summing over a geometric grid of radii; monotonicity extends the conclusion to intermediate radii.
The proof also removes a finite union of boundary circles, a null set.
This uses the disc variance clause directly rather than Corollary 5.4.

nodes.title: BRS second moment with one frequency fixed
nodes.summary: The fixed-height signed-frequency second moment used as Theorem 2.1.

references.locator: Theorem 1.3; Section 2.1 for the small-power convention

nodes.title: Selberg identity for integer Kloosterman arguments
nodes.summary: Elementary proof cited for equation (2.4); v39 gives no numbered locator for this citation.

references.locator: Paper cited without a numbered locator

nodes.title: Divisor small-power bound
nodes.summary: For each positive eta, tau(v)<<_eta v^eta.

nodes.title: Ramanujan-sum identity
nodes.summary: The divisor expression for Ramanujan sums used to bound the coordinate axes.

nodes.title: Summatory totient estimate
nodes.summary: Mertens's estimate gives N_X=(3/pi^2)X^2+O(X log X).

nodes.title: Parseval identity on the torus
nodes.summary: The L2 norm is the sum of squared Fourier coefficients.

nodes.title: Fourier inversion for smooth periodic functions
nodes.summary: Rapid coefficient decay and absolute uniform Fourier inversion for smooth torus functions.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a convolution
nodes.summary: Convolution multiplies Fourier coefficients.

nodes.title: Fourier transform of the modular inverse point set
nodes.summary: The finite exponential sum over $\mathcal P_X$ equals $A_X(m,n)=\sum_{c\le X}S(m,n;c)$, with every point counted once and the modulus-one point represented by $S(m,n;1)=1$.

nodes.title: Point-set cardinality and quadratic scale
nodes.summary: The point count is $N_X=\sum_{c\le X}\varphi(c)=(3/\pi^2)X^2+O(X\log X)$; in particular $N_X\asymp X^2$ for $X\ge2$.
notes: The lower bound is recalled immediately before Corollary 2.4 at line 452.

nodes.title: Trivial bound for normalized point coefficients
nodes.summary: The normalized coefficients satisfy $a_X(k)=N_X^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal P_X}e(k\cdot z)$, $a_X(0)=1$ and $|a_X(k)|\le1$.
notes: Used again at line 470 and in the convergence assertion of Proposition 3.1(iii).

nodes.title: Interchange and simultaneous sign reversal
nodes.summary: The elementary changes of variables give $S(m,n;c)=S(n,m;c)$ and $S(-m,-n;c)=S(m,n;c)$.

nodes.title: Selberg's identity for Kloosterman sums
nodes.summary: For integers $m,n$ and $c\ge1$, $S(m,n;c)=\sum_{d\mid\gcd(m,n,c)}d\,S(mn/d^2,1;c/d)$.

references.locator: Paper cited without a numbered locator
Paper cited without a numbered locator
Paper cited without a numbered locator

notes: v39 cites Xi as a whole paper; it does not give the equation locator used in the other manuscript.

nodes.title: Cumulative Selberg identity
nodes.summary: For $mn\ne0$, summing Selberg's identity over the modulus gives $A_X(m,n)=\sum_{d\mid\gcd(|m|,|n|),\,d\le X}d\,A_{X/d}(mn/d^2,1)$.

nodes.title: Small-power divisor estimate
nodes.summary: For every $\eta>0$ and integer $v\ge1$, $\tau(v)\ll_\eta v^\eta$.

nodes.title: Off-axis reduction of the rectangular second moment
nodes.summary: Cauchy–Schwarz over divisors and at most $2\tau(|r|)$ signed factorizations $uv=r$ reduce the off-axis second moment to $\sum_{d\le\min(M,N,X)}d^2\sum_{1\le|r|\le MN/d^2}|A_{X/d}(r,1)|^2$. The cumulative input applies with $R=MN/d^2\ge1$, $Y=X/d\ge1$; the divisor sums have weights $d^{-2}$ and $d^{-1}$.
notes: The divisor cutoff prevents any use of the cited moment bound below height one.
This is the off-axis component of Proposition 2.3, not a separate numbered result.

nodes.title: Axis contribution from Ramanujan sums
nodes.summary: The Ramanujan formula $S(0,n;c)=\sum_{d\mid\gcd(c,n)}d\mu(c/d)$ gives $|A_X(0,n)|\le X\tau(|n|)$; symmetry gives the corresponding bound on the other axis. The divisor estimate then bounds both axes by $O_\eta(MNX^2(MN)^{2\eta})$.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a translate
nodes.summary: With $\widehat f(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^2}f(x)e(-k\cdot x)\,dx$, one has $\widehat{f(\cdot+h)}(k)=e(k\cdot h)\widehat f(k)$.
notes: Recalled with the other Fourier facts at line 477.

nodes.title: Positive periodic mollifier and Fourier decay
nodes.summary: For $0<\delta\le1/8$, the periodized mollifier $\rho_\delta$ is nonnegative, has integral one and support within distance $\delta$ of zero. Integration by parts proves $|\widehat{\rho_\delta}(k)|\ll_L(1+\delta\|k\|_\infty)^{-L}$ for every $L>0$.

nodes.title: Boundary crossing along a short torus path
nodes.summary: A shortest lifted segment joining a point of $E$ to a point of $E^c$ meets $\partial E$. Applied to the inner and outer sets used for smoothing, this places their indicator differences from $\mathbf1_E$ within the $3\delta$ boundary neighborhood.
notes: The same path argument is reused in Remark 2.9 for a translation; the numerical content of Lemma 2.5 is not involved.

nodes.title: Boundary-neighborhood control of smoothing errors
nodes.summary: For the inner and outer sets $E_\pm$, $\|\mathbf1_{E_\pm}-\mathbf1_E\|_1\le b_E(3\delta)$ and $\|\mathbf1_{E_\pm}-\mathbf1_E\|_2^2\le b_E(3\delta)$.

nodes.title: Elementary boundary geometry for a convex set
nodes.summary: For a convex body in a unit square, the boundary is a rectifiable Jordan curve of length $P\le4$. The arc covering argument shows that it has measure zero, while convexity gives $\operatorname{int}\overline\Omega\subset\Omega$. Thus $\mathbf1_\Omega=\mathbf1_{\overline\Omega}$ almost everywhere. Degenerate sets are handled separately.
notes: The coordinate-width proof of P≤4 is at line 591; the null-boundary conclusion is at line 597; segments, points and the empty set are discussed at line 614.
This auxiliary geometric foundation is proved in the manuscript, not imported from the introductory Fourier-decay literature.

nodes.title: Boundary tube bound for a projected convex set
nodes.summary: For $E=\pi\Omega$ with convex $\Omega\subset u+[0,1)^2$, $b_E(s)\le4\pi(Ps+s^2)$ for $0<s\le1$. A cover of the Euclidean boundary is projected to the torus, using $\partial E\subset\pi(\partial\overline\Omega)$ and that projection does not increase measure.
notes: The statement is at line 581; degenerate cases are proved at line 614.

nodes.title: Convex translation estimate with constant one
nodes.summary: Parallel-line slicing gives $|(K+h)\triangle K|\le P|h|_2$, since the perpendicular width is at most $P/2$. Periodization then yields $\|\mathbf1_E(\cdot+h)-\mathbf1_E\|_2^2\le P|h|_2$ on the torus for every $h\in\mathbb R^2$.
notes: The statement is at line 582; the null-boundary reduction is used explicitly at line 603; degenerate cases are at line 614.

nodes.title: Fourier-energy tail for a convex indicator
nodes.summary: The translation estimate with $\Lambda=P$ and $\alpha=1$ in Lemma 2.5 yields $\sum_{\|k\|_\infty\ge T}|\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(k)|^2\ll P/T$ for $T\ge1$, and hence the same bound on a dyadic shell.
notes: The statement is at lines 583 and 586.

nodes.title: Pointwise Fourier decay for a convex indicator
nodes.summary: For $k\ne0$, the special translation $h=k/(2|k|_2^2)$ has multiplier $-2$ and gives $|\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(k)|\le P/(4|k|_2)$. Combining this with the trivial area bound gives $\min\{A,P/(4|k|_2)\}$.
notes: The statement is at line 584. The notation |k|_2 is Euclidean length, not the second coordinate.

nodes.title: Smooth Fourier identity for uniform counting
nodes.summary: For smooth $f$, $\int f\,d\mu_X-\int f=\sum_{k\ne0}\widehat f(k)a_X(k)$, with absolute convergence. It follows by pointwise smooth Fourier inversion and a finite average over $\mathcal P_X$.
notes: The statement is at lines 643–647.

nodes.title: Smooth Fourier identity for the difference measure
nodes.summary: For smooth $f$, $\int f\,d\nu_X-\int f=\sum_{k\ne0}\widehat f(k)|a_X(k)|^2$, with absolute convergence. The finite double exponential sum factors as $a_X(k)\overline{a_X(k)}$.
notes: The statement is at lines 648–652. This does not require the numerical difference-distribution theorem.

nodes.title: Parseval identity for translation variance
nodes.summary: For every measurable $E$, the finite reflected-translate sum $Z_E(u)=\mu_X(u+E)-|E|$ has nonzero Fourier coefficients $a_X(-k)\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(-k)$. Parseval gives $\mathcal V_X(E)=\sum_{k\ne0}|\widehat{\mathbf1_E}(k)|^2|a_X(k)|^2$.
notes: The statement and convergence justification are at lines 653–657; |a_X(k)|≤1 bounds the series by the indicator's L² energy.

nodes.title: Variance is unchanged by null-set changes
nodes.summary: The variance identity depends only on the $L^2$ class of $\mathbf1_E$, so changing $E$ on a null set leaves $\mathcal V_X(E)$ unchanged. In particular, boundary choices do not affect convex-set variance.

nodes.title: Equality of translation norms for indicators
nodes.summary: For an indicator, $\|\mathbf1_E(\cdot+h)-\mathbf1_E\|_2^2=\|\mathbf1_E(\cdot+h)-\mathbf1_E\|_1=|(E-h)\triangle E|$.
notes: Used to apply the L² translation lemma to geometric symmetric-difference bounds.

nodes.title: From pointwise brackets to a Fourier discrepancy bound
nodes.summary: Pointwise upper and lower brackets reduce discrepancy to the larger smooth counting Fourier sum plus their integral error. The same reduction applies to general measurable sets.
notes: The displayed convex specialization is equation (4.2). Line 883 explicitly reuses the argument with boundary error $3B\delta^{\alpha}$.
This auxiliary node records the generic reduction proved by the argument, not a new numbered result.
No convex error estimate is built into this node; it is supplied separately in each application.

nodes.title: Injective coordinate projections and counting in short intervals
nodes.summary: Distinct points have distinct coordinates; their lifts have coordinate spacing at least $X^{-2}$. A width-$w_j$ interval therefore contains at most $1+w_jX^2$ lifted points.
notes: This is denominator arithmetic for the specific point set, not an application of a cited Farey discrepancy theorem.
The coordinate injectivity and count are proved separately for the two coordinates.

nodes.title: Combining geometric and Fourier discrepancy estimates
nodes.summary: Takes the smaller of the coordinate-width bound and the perimeter-sensitive Fourier bound.

nodes.title: Elementary upper bound for the point count
nodes.summary: The identity $N_X=\sum_{c\le X}\varphi(c)$ and $\varphi(c)\le c$ give $N_X\le X^2$ for $X\ge1$. This elementary upper bound is used in the small-perimeter examples and repeated in the lower distance estimate.
notes: The printed calculation is made for integer X. The point set and its cardinality depend only on floor(X), so the same upper bound holds for real X>=1.
Do not replace this elementary input by the full summatory-totient asymptotic merely because the latter also appears in the introduction.

nodes.title: Diagonal segments realizing the short-perimeter lower order
nodes.summary: A segment starting at $(1/X,1/X)$ captures both one point and a number proportional to $pX^2$; division by $N_X$ gives the two terms in the lower bound. Integer parts handle real heights.
notes: The segment perimeter is twice its length, as required by the manuscript's degenerate-perimeter convention.
At p=0 the segment is a single point.

nodes.title: From boundary tubes to Fourier and bracket norms
nodes.summary: A path crossing the topological boundary bounds the symmetric difference by $B|h|_2^{\alpha}$; the translation lemma and smooth brackets then give shell norms uniformly in alpha.
notes: The method borrowed from Remark 2.9 is the boundary-crossing containment, not its linear-in-|h| conclusion.
The translation lemma's explicit constant is uniformly bounded for $0<\alpha\le1$.
The bracket error is at most $3B\delta^{\alpha}$.

nodes.title: Dyadic summation uniform in the boundary exponent
nodes.summary: Uses the explicit geometric-series constants for exponents in compact positive ranges, and treats $\beta=1/3-\alpha/2$ directly through zero with a logarithmic cutoff factor.
notes: Lemma 4.1's statement does not cover exponent zero and its arbitrary-s constant alone does not supply alpha-uniformity.
The direct near-zero estimate is substantive support for the epsilon-only constant in Theorem 1.4.

nodes.title: Smoothing estimate for a general boundary tube bound
nodes.summary: Combines the pointwise discrepancy reduction, boundary-based bracket norms, arithmetic shell estimate and uniform dyadic sums before optimizing delta.
notes: This estimate has a constant independent of alpha, B, E, X and delta, apart from its stated dependence on eta.
It is proved anew; the convex numerical estimate of Proposition 4.2 is not invoked.

nodes.title: From Euclidean well-shapedness to torus boundary control
nodes.summary: Separates a strip near the unit-square boundary from interior discs to obtain $b_{\pi\Omega}(s)\le(8+4\gamma)s$ at small s, and an admissible global constant $B=8(1+\gamma)$ for alpha one.
notes: This uses the pointwise definition of the topological boundary, not a boundary chosen up to a null set.
The same linear tube consequence is later used to rule out well-shapedness of the Koch example.

nodes.title: Tube control for a Koch boundary
nodes.summary: The construction arcs give a covering by $O((\ell/s)^d)$ discs of radius $O(s)$, yielding boundary-tube order at most $s^{2-d}$; the source's dimension d also obstructs a linear tube bound.
notes: The domain closure lies strictly inside the unit square, so sufficiently small Euclidean neighborhoods project injectively.
Uses the construction and dimension from LP; no convex-set Fourier or tube estimate is applied.
The two conclusions in Remark 4.7 use this upper tube estimate and the dimension information in different directions.

notes: This node imports a definition. It does not import the earlier discrepancy bound or the assertion that convex sets are well-shaped.

nodes.title: Convex difference estimate from pointwise brackets and squared shells
nodes.summary: Bracket the convex indicator pointwise, use the nonnegative coefficients $|a_X(k)|^2$ in the difference identity, sum the squared shell estimates, and take $\delta=(8X)^{-1}$ to obtain the convex clause of Theorem 1.5.
notes: Proposition 4.2 supplies the earlier pattern of the smoothing reduction, but its numerical discrepancy estimate is not a proof input here.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of an arc indicator
nodes.summary: Direct integration gives the nonzero coefficient of an arc indicator as an endpoint exponential difference divided by $2\pi i m$. Its modulus is bounded by the smaller of the arc length and $(\pi|m|)^{-1}$; the zero coefficient is the length.
notes: This shared calculation is used in the bracket proof and, without smoothing, in the rectangle variance proof.

nodes.title: Product brackets and separate frequency summation for differences
nodes.summary: Use products of arc brackets and dyadic blocks in each frequency separately. Proposition 2.3 and the resulting one-variable sums, with $\delta=(16X^2)^{-1}$, give the area-dependent rectangle clause of Theorem 1.5.
notes: The frequency blocks and factorized summation are later reused as a method in the rectangle variance proof.

nodes.title: Removing equal-point pairs
nodes.summary: The exact relation $\nu_X=(1-N_X^{-1})\nu_X^*+N_X^{-1}\delta_0$ implies that the two probability measures differ on any measurable set by at most $N_X^{-1}\ll X^{-2}$.
notes: The identity is independent of Theorem 1.5; combining them gives its distinct-pair extension.

nodes.title: Convex variance from Fourier tails and squared shells
nodes.summary: Handle sets below the one-point threshold by the exact identity. Otherwise split at frequency $T=X^2/P$, use the convex Fourier tail above $T$, and pair the pointwise coefficient bound with the squared shell estimate below $T$.
notes: The proof uses both clauses of Lemma 2.7 concerning Fourier coefficients, together with the elementary perimeter and width bounds.

nodes.title: Disc variance as a convex-set specialization
nodes.summary: Apply the established convex variance estimate with area $\pi r^2$ and perimeter $2\pi r$; discs of radius at most $1/4$ fit in a translated unit square.

nodes.title: Rectangle variance from squared arc coefficients
nodes.summary: Use the one-point identity for a side below $X^{-2}$. Otherwise factor the squared indicator coefficients, sum separate frequency blocks against Proposition 2.3, and split the one-variable sums at the reciprocal side lengths.
notes: The formula for raw arc coefficients comes from the calculation in Lemma 5.1's proof; the smooth bracket estimate itself is not needed.
The numerical difference estimate is not used.

nodes.title: An explicit empty rectangle at scale X to the minus one half
nodes.summary: For $X>9$, the rectangle $[2X^{-1/2},3X^{-1/2}]\times[\tfrac15X^{-1/2},\tfrac14X^{-1/2}]$ has area $1/(20X)$ and contains no modular-inverse point. The proof separates points with $ab=1$ from those with $ab=1+jc$, $j\ge1$.

references.role: method origin; explicit case proved in v39

notes: BRS Section 1.2 is credited for the empty-box construction; this particular rectangle is verified directly in v39.
This node is a proof input for the distance lower bound and also explains the uniform shrinking-set obstruction.

nodes.title: Distance tail from the disc variance
nodes.summary: An empty disc forces normalized-count deviation $\pi r^2$. Chebyshev's inequality and the disc variance therefore bound the measure of $\{d_X>r\}$ by $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(X^{-2}r^{-2}+X^{-5/3}r^{-2/3})$ for $0<r\le1/4$.

nodes.title: Uniform distance cutoff from shrinking-set equidistribution
nodes.summary: For any fixed $0<\kappa\le1/4$ and sufficiently large $X$, Corollary 1.3 ensures that every disc of radius $X^{-1/2+\kappa}$ contains a point. Hence $d_X(u)<X^{-1/2+\kappa}$ for every center.
notes: This is an actual dependence on Corollary 1.3, not an elementary Farey covering argument.

nodes.title: Integrating the distance tail up to its uniform cutoff
nodes.summary: Use the layer-cake formula, the trivial tail bound below $X^{-1}$, the variance tail up to $X^{-1/2+\kappa}$, and the vanishing tail beyond it. The integral of $r^{s-3}$ produces the three cases $s<2$, $s=2$, and $s>2$.
notes: At $s=2$ the integration produces a logarithm which is absorbed together with the pre-existing epsilon loss; no exact logarithmic order is established.

nodes.title: Packing and the empty rectangle give the two distance lower bounds
nodes.summary: A union of $N_X$ discs covering at most half the torus gives a lower bound $\gg_sX^{-s}$. The middle quarter of the explicit empty rectangle has measure $\asymp X^{-1}$ and distance $\gg X^{-1/2}$ from the point set, giving $\gg_sX^{-1-s/2}$.
notes: The packing estimate only needs the elementary inequality $N_X\le X^2$, proved in the displayed argument; it does not require Mertens's asymptotic.

notes: The edge to the explicitly verified rectangle is method attribution. The local-statistics proof does not import the emptiness of this particular rectangle as an unproved external assertion.

comparisons.title: First moment on a frequency shell
comparisons.summary: The shell first moment satisfies $\sum_{k\in\mathscr H(H)}|a_X(k)|\ll_\eta(HX)^\eta(X^{-1}H^2+X^{-5/6}H^{4/3})$. The text cites BRS and also gives the alternative derivation by Cauchy–Schwarz from Corollary 2.4.
notes: The subsequent BRS Section 5.1, Section 5.4 and equation (3.5) citations explain earlier discrepancy methods; they are not prerequisites of the new theorems.

comparisons.title: Discrepancy obtained from the shell first moment
comparisons.summary: Pairing the maximal bracket coefficient with the shell first moment yields $D_X(E)\ll_\eta b+(X/\delta)^\eta(PX^{-1}\delta^{-1}+PX^{-5/6}\delta^{-1/3}+bX^{-1}\delta^{-2}+bX^{-5/6}\delta^{-4/3})$, where $b=P\delta+\delta^2$. At $\delta=X^{-1/2}$, $X\ge64$, this is $\ll_\varepsilon X^\varepsilon(PX^{-1/2}+X^{-1})$.
notes: This is a comparison bound, not an intermediate premise of the sharper perimeter theorem.
The cited dyadic sums are outlined in Section 1; the later dyadic-summation lemma need not be made an input merely because it proves a reusable version.

comparisons.title: Height variance obtained by averaging fixed-modulus standard deviations
comparisons.summary: Writing $\mu_X=N_X^{-1}\sum_{c\le X}\varphi(c)\mu_c$, the triangle inequality and Humphries's disc variance bound give $\mathcal V_X(B_r)^{1/2}\ll_\varepsilon rN_X^{-1}\sum_{c\le X}\varphi(c)^{1/2}c^\varepsilon\ll_\varepsilon rX^{-1/2+\varepsilon}$. Thus $\mathcal V_X(B_r)\ll_\varepsilon r^2X^{-1+2\varepsilon}$.

notes: This comparison is not used to prove Theorem 1.6; the following comparison with Theorem 1.6 is not a reverse proof dependency.

discussion.title: The exponent 2/3
discussion.summary: The two leading terms in the existing smoothing argument balance at exponent 2/3. Removing the sharp-cutoff term alone would not improve that balance. The text suggests additional geometric or arithmetic input and leaves the gap between the known convex-discrepancy lower and upper bounds unresolved.
notes: This is not an optimality theorem for all possible methods.

discussion.title: The mean-spacing scale
discussion.summary: The proved difference and variance bounds reach relative asymptotics above X inverse by a fixed power. At mean spacing they provide upper bounds but no limiting law. The text identifies pair correlation at mean spacing as a further question and cites the announced Blomer preprint as context.

references.locator: Announced preprint; no theorem locator in v39

notes: The exact one-point identity concerns the smaller width scale below X to the minus two.

discussion.title: Other test sets
discussion.summary: The aspect-ratio-independent area bounds are established for products of coordinate arcs; their validity for arbitrary rotated rectangles is left open. The text also sketches a controlled-boundary extension of the difference method with error B X to the minus alpha plus epsilon and explicitly leaves its details and fractal-boundary local statistics to future work.
notes: The sketched controlled-boundary estimate is an unnumbered discussion claim, not an additional proved numbered result in this inventory.

discussion.title: The second moment of the distance
discussion.status: Unresolved subpower factor and leading constant
discussion.summary: For s=2, Theorem 1.7 gives lower order X to the minus two and upper order X to the minus two plus epsilon. The source leaves the remaining factor and constant undetermined and relates the issue to empty discs across the range from mean spacing to the empty-rectangle scale.
notes: The logarithm appearing in an upper-bound integration does not establish an exact logarithmic order.

literature_notes: The proof graph starts from the frequency moment as packaged in BRS Theorem 1.3. The spectral ancestry of that result, including Kuznetsov and the Deshouillers–Iwaniec large sieve, is not expanded into additional premises for this paper.

Selberg38 gives the historical attribution for Selberg's identity; Kuznetsov and Xi are the proof references cited in v39. The graph uses Xi as the explicit literature input and keeps the other references on the identity record. BRS Section 4.1 is credited for the general-frequency reduction. The empty-box construction is credited to BRS Section 1.2, while the particular rectangle used in the distance proof is verified directly in v39.

BRS's earlier discrepancy bounds, first moments, dyadic packing method and general lower bounds are used for comparisons. The BRS Section 3.1 definition of well-shapedness is an input, but the nearby earlier well-shaped discrepancy estimate is not. Humphries's fixed-modulus variance enters a comparison calculation in Section 3.3, not the proof of Theorem 1.6.

The angular Fourier-decay results of Podkorytov and Brandolini–Colzani–Travaglini, the geometric-discrepancy literature including Colzani–Gigante–Travaglini, and the earlier Farey, discrepancy and Kloosterman results provide context. The manuscript proves its own translation, tube and bracket estimates. The announced Blomer pair-correlation preprint is contextual and is described here only as v39 describes it; it is not a proof input.
